title: The Ray Aspect of Light
lead: Light gets from a source to another place in three ways: directly through empty space, through media such as air and glass, or after reflecting from something such as a mirror. In every case it travels in straight lines called rays, changing direction only where it meets an object or passes into another material. That picture holds whenever light meets objects several times as large as its wavelength. The part of optics built on it is geometric optics, with its two laws of reflection and refraction.
objectives: List the ways by which light travels from a source to another location.
summary_html:
• A straight line that originates at some point is called a ray.
  • The part of optics dealing with the ray aspect of light is called geometric optics.
  • Light can travel in three ways from a source to another location: (1) directly from the source through empty space; (2) through various media; (3) after being reflected from a mirror.
notes: The module’s one problem, the full-length mirror, needs the law of reflection and is set with 25.2, where that law is introduced.

figures.original_caption: Three methods for light to travel from a source to another location. (a) Light reaches the upper atmosphere of Earth traveling through empty space directly from the source. (b) Light can reach a person in one of two ways. It can travel through media like air and glass. It can also reflect from an object like a mirror. In the situations shown here, light interacts with objects large enough that it travels in straight lines, like a ray.

exercises.prompt: When light from a distant object reflects off of a concave mirror and comes to a focus some distance in front of the mirror, we model light as a _____ to explain and predict the behavior of light and the formation of an image.

answer.hint: A mirror is many times as large as the wavelength of light, so the light reflecting from it travels in straight lines.

exercises.prompt: Light of wavelength 500 nm is incident on a narrow slit of width 150 nm. Which model of light most accurately predicts the behavior of the light after it passes through the slit? Explain your answer.

answer.solution: The wave model. Light acts like a ray only when it interacts with objects several times as large as its wavelength. Here the slit, 150 nm wide, is narrower than the 500 nm wavelength, so the wave characteristics of the light are pronounced: the light spreads out on the far side of the slit rather than continuing in a straight line, and the ray model cannot predict that.
